headline: Sonos unveils new headphones, soundbar, and AI-powered software updates
summary: The audio giant is betting big on artificial intelligence with its new Sonos 27 operating system, alongside new hardware.
details: Sonos has announced its most significant product and software update in years, introducing the Sonos Ace Ultra headphones and Beam Ultra soundbar. The company is also rolling out Sonos 27, a major update to its operating system that heavily integrates AI for enhanced user control and customization.

The new Sonos 27 OS features an in-house developed voice assistant for music and system control, set to launch in early access this fall. Additionally, Sonos 27mcp will allow users to connect existing AI models like ChatGPT and Google Gemini, with custom agent creation capabilities coming in 2027.

Users will be able to create up to 10 custom AI agents with distinct voices and roles, offering personalized interactions for tasks like receiving news updates or motivational prompts. This deep AI integration aims to expand the customization and control options beyond the current app capabilities.

Hardware updates include the Sonos Ace Ultra headphones, designed to be a seamless part of the Sonos ecosystem. The Beam Ultra soundbar also joins the product lineup, promising enhanced audio experiences.

Sonos is also enhancing its Fabric whole-home system. Wireless Play and Move 2 speakers can now function as surround sound speakers, automatically configuring to their new roles. Compatible Sonos headphones will integrate into home systems, enabling seamless audio transfer between speakers and headphones, rolling out September 29th.

The Sonos app is receiving significant UI improvements, including new Home, System, and Search tabs, and a customizable room sort option. A virtual volume knob controlled by two fingers adds a unique, tactile element, rolling out September 8th for iOS users first.

Lockscreen controls for volume and playback are returning to the app, having started rolling out on August 17th. System health views and presets are also planned for release later this fall, further improving user troubleshooting and system management.

headline_marked: Nvidia DLSS 5 [[launches September 3]] with NBA 2K27, requires RTX 50 series
headline: Nvidia DLSS 5 launches September 3 with NBA 2K27, requires RTX 50 series
summary: Nvidia's controversial DLSS 5, dubbed "3D-guided Neural Rendering," officially launches September 3rd with NBA 2K27. The AI-powered graphics technology will be exclusive to RTX 50 series GPUs and GeForce NOW, and early benchmarks suggest it may significantly i
details: Nvidia has confirmed that its controversial DLSS 5 technology will launch on September 3rd at 9 PM PT, with NBA 2K27 being the first game to support it. The feature will be available for all RTX 50 Series GPUs, laptops, and GeForce NOW users.

DLSS 5, officially named "3D-guided Neural Rendering," aims to enhance visual realism by simulating natural light interactions with game elements like hair and skin, using AI trained on real-world data. Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang described it as "the GPT moment for graphics."

Despite the visual enhancements, DLSS 5 has faced criticism due to its AI-driven nature and potential performance impacts. Early indications suggest that enabling the technology could lead to significant drops in frame rates.

The technology's exclusivity to the RTX 50 series GPUs and GeForce NOW means older graphics cards will not benefit from DLSS 5. Nvidia has released initial benchmarks showing 4K performance on the RTX 5090 and 5080, though results on less powerful cards remain unclear.
While NBA 2K27 might seem an unusual choice for a launch title, Nvidia claims close collaboration with Visual Concepts and 2K to achieve a "new level of authentic sports experience."
